chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who desires that he should have a pregnancy (offspring), let him pray two Rak'at after the Friday prayer, prolonging in them the bowing and prostration.
Then he should say: O Allah! I ask You by what Zakariyya asked You when he said: My Lord! Do not leave me alone (without offspring), and You are the Best of inheritors.
O Allah! Grant me a goodly offspring, surely You are the Hearer of the supplication.

O Allah! By Your Name I have made her permissible (for intercourse), and in Your Trust I have taken her. So if You decree a child in her womb, then make it a boy, and do not make for the Satan any share or partnership in him.

key_terms.اسْتَحْلَلْتُهَا: I made her permissible (for marital relations)
key_terms.يُحْبَلَ: to become pregnant / to have offspring

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for having children in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith outlines a specific Sunnah prayer for conception, linking the supplicant to the lineage of Prophet Zakariyya (AS) to emphasize divine responsiveness to earnest pleas for progeny. The ritual involves prolonging Ruku and Sujud to cultivate humility, followed by a dua that not only requests a righteous child but also seeks protection from Shaytan's influence, reflecting the Shia emphasis on spiritual purity in the domestic sphere. This practice underscores the integration of physical intention with spiritual devotion in seeking Allah's blessing for family continuity.
